description: We are Team Innovative Minds from  India - a group of students passionate about space education and storytelling. We love building simple, kid-friendly tech with HTML, CSS, JS and NASA open data. Our project ECHOES turns 800+ abandoned Moon & Mars hardware into cute Pixar-like characters teaching science to kids 7-14 yrs. We are looking for teammates who like design, storytelling, and making space fun for schools. Join us!
summary: An interactive storybook where NASA's discarded Moon & Mars hardware become cute Pixar-like characters teaching science to school kids.
details:
Since the nineteen sixties humanity has left over eight hundred objects on the Moon and Mars including derelict equipment, spent hardware, and trash, and these objects are not just junk but historical heroes at risk. School kids find space boring because there is lack of engaging content connecting them to real missions, and youth interest in STEM is dropping by forty two percent, especially in Indian government schools where regional language interactive content is missing.

Our solution is ECHOES which is an interactive storybook website where discarded hardware becomes cute Pixar-like characters who tell their own stories in first person, making science fun and emotional for kids from seven to fourteen years old. We created eight heroes including Opportunity rover who said my battery is low and it is getting dark and lived fifteen years versus ninety days planned, Apollo eleven mirror which is still working after fifty seven years and measures Moon moving 3.8 centimeters per year away from Earth, Apollo fourteen golf balls where Alan Shepard hit miles and miles in low gravity, Ingenuity helicopter which planned five flights but flew seventy two times as first aircraft on another planet, Apollo seventeen lunar rover which drove thirty five kilometers and found orange volcanic glass soil, Voyager one which is now twenty four billion kilometers away in interstellar space carrying Golden Record with greetings for aliens, ninety six bags of trash including poop left to bring three hundred eighty two kilograms Moon rocks which is now future biology experiment, and Spirit rover which got stuck but never gave up and became stationary lab finding hot springs.

We tested this in schools and kids loved it especially the Moon poop story which helps them remember science tradeoffs, and our website is single file HTML CSS JS with zero backend, works on any phone, offline ready, perfect for low bandwidth schools, and uses only NASA open data for Global Award eligibility. They are abandoned but with ECHOES they are NOT forgotten and we give voice to forgotten heroes so next generation of Moon explorers will remember them. Team Innovative Minds,India
